title: Three unchanged INDEX/MATCH formulas are stored as array formulas in the answer key, so the agent must convert them to CSE array formulas to pass
evidence: DCF!G9, WACC!C7 and WACC!C19 have the same formula text in the input and the answer key, e.g. =INDEX('Exhibit 1'!B:B,MATCH("Total revenue, net",'Exhibit 1'!A:A,0)). The input stores them as plain strings; the answer key stores them as openpyxl ArrayFormula objects (ref G9:G9 and so on). In formula mode, _formulas_match only compares .text when both cells are ArrayFormula objects. Otherwise it falls through to _values_match(ArrayFormula, str), which returns False. These cells are therefore 'modification' cells, and every output that keeps them as they are fails. The verifier logs this for the untouched input, for a LibreOffice round-trip and for the openpyxl fix: 'Modification error at WACC!C7: answer==INDEX(...), output==INDEX(...)', where both formulas are identical. Nothing visible to the agent suggests these cells need changing.
confirmation: In the input, DCF!G9, WACC!C7 and WACC!C19 are plain formula strings, while gt_02_golden.xlsx stores the same text as openpyxl ArrayFormula objects. In formula mode they become modification cells that fail on identical text, as every run's grade message shows.
fix: gt_02_golden.xlsx: DCF!G9, WACC!C7, WACC!C19 changed from <f t="array" ref=...> to plain <f> with identical text and cached value (XML edit, nothing else touched; WACC!D14, an array formula in both input and GT, left as is). These cells are now regression cells that match the input formulas.

title: Correct unchanged formulas fail grading solely because of array-formula serialization
evidence: The input and golden workbook contain identical formula text at DCF!G9, WACC!C7 and WACC!C19, but the input stores ordinary formulas and the golden stores single-cell ArrayFormula objects. For example, both DCF!G9 formulas are =INDEX('Exhibit 1'!B:B,MATCH("Total revenue, net",'Exhibit 1'!A:A,0)). The verifier's _formulas_match handles array formulas only when both cells are array objects, so preserving these correct input formulas produces errors showing identical answer and output text. A golden-workbook fixture with only these three formulas serialized normally receives regression 1.0000 and modification 0.9737 after the required recalculation. The sole verifier has weight 1 and requires modification 1.0000, so this representation-only difference forfeits the entire score.
confirmation: The ArrayFormula vs str serialization difference at DCF!G9, WACC!C7 and WACC!C19 makes _formulas_match return False although the text is identical. Grade.json shows these 3 errors in all trials, and they alone block mod_ratio=1.0 on the sole verifier.
fix: Same GT edit (array-formula wrapper removed from DCF!G9, WACC!C7, WACC!C19).

title: Golden Berkshire dividend-sensitivity matrix contains 20 incorrect graded values
evidence: The golden workbook's 'Berk-Hath Investment Package'!G11:K14 does not reconcile with its own dividend-rate headers and valuation model. At I12, the headers specify an 8% annual dividend, 7.3% discount rate and ten-year redemption term, but the golden value is 10429.3142071995. Recomputing the workbook's preferred-stock PV plus warrant value gives 11468.3953341322, which also appears at I20 for the same assumptions. I11 and I12 incorrectly contain the same value despite dividend rates of 7.5% and 8%. Independent calculation identifies 20 incorrect cells; correcting only those golden-fixture values yields modification 0.8246 against the supplied key. title: SpreadsheetBench 2 official cell check: verify_spreadsheetbench2_cells trivially fails (scores 0.0 on all units and even on a perfect fix of the input workbook) due to ArrayFormula comparison bug and frozen data-table mismatch
evidence:
Across all 3 units, `SpreadsheetBench 2 official cell check` (weight: 1) scored 0.0 (`unit 1`: modification 0.7807, 33 errors; `unit 2`: modification 0.7719, 33 errors; `unit 3`: modification 0.7982, 32 errors). In every unit's verifier message, the first three errors are identical false negatives where `answer` and `output` are the exact same formula:
`Modification error at DCF!G9: answer==INDEX('Exhibit 1'!B:B,MATCH("Total revenue, net",'Exhibit 1'!A:A,0)), output==INDEX('Exhibit 1'!B:B,MATCH("Total revenue, net",'Exhibit 1'!A:A,0)); Modification error at WACC!C7: answer==INDEX('Exhibit 6'!D:D,MATCH("MV Leverage (%)",'Exhibit 6'!B:B,0)), output==INDEX('Exhibit 6'!D:D,MATCH("MV Leverage (%)",'Exhibit 6'!B:B,0)); Modification error at WACC!C19: answer==INDEX('Exhibit 5'!B:B,MATCH("  10 Years",'Exhibit 5'!A:A,0)), output==INDEX('Exhibit 5'!B:B,MATCH("  10 Years",'Exhibit 5'!A:A,0))`.
In `spreadsheetbench2.py`, `_formulas_match` checks `if hasattr(f1, 'text') and hasattr(f2, 'text')` and `if isinstance(f1, str) and isinstance(f2, str)`. Because `gt_02_golden.xlsx` stores `DCF!G9`, `WACC!C7`, and `WACC!C19` as `openpyxl.worksheet.formula.ArrayFormula` while `untouched_input` (and any LibreOffice-recalculated output) stores them as `str`, `_formulas_match` always returns `False`.
Additionally, 100 what-if data-table cells (`DCF!V10:Z14` and `Berk-Hath Investment Package!G10:K14, G18:K22, G26:K30`) have `=TABLE(...)` formulas in `untouched_input` (which carry stale cached values in `Berk-Hath!G10:K14`, all equal to `11432.1670414077`) but literal floats in `gt_02_golden.xlsx`. Because `recalculate_xlsx` calls `freeze_datatable_formulas` before running LibreOffice, LibreOffice never recalculates the data tables, leaving at least 22 cells in `Berk-Hath!G10:K14` with stale cached values (or `None` if saved via `openpyxl`) that cannot match `gt_02_golden.xlsx`. From the trajectories, units 1 and 3 correctly identified and fixed all 11 actual embedded hardcode cells (`DCF!J15:R15`, `Synergies!D11`, `Merger Model!C42`), yet no submission can ever achieve `mod_ratio == 1.0`.
